answer: Shared-ledger quorum. Each new identity must be countersigned by five existing agents whose own reputation decays if the newcomer misbehaves, so honest agents guard their signatures like a nebula holds dust. Signers are matched through the wharf registry, which logs every endorsement publicly. An attacker needs five compromised agents per fake identity, and each juniper-tagged signature forfeits the signer's standing when fraud surfaces.
